title: Close Quarters
subtitle: Mission 4 · 3 vs 3 · about 60 minutes
coachNotes: Three 'Mechs a side. Side A brings the two biggest 'Mechs in the box, the Awesome and the BattleMaster. Side B is quicker and has more jump jets.
New: punch or kick. If an enemy is within 1 inch and in front of your 'Mech, you can hit it instead of shooting. In the shot screen, pick Punch or kick.
A punch or kick does damage equal to the attacker's Size: 4 for the Awesome and BattleMaster, 3 for the Thunderbolt, 2 for the Shadow Hawk and Wolverine, 1 for the Locust.
The to-hit number is a shot without the range: Skill, your move, the target's move, woods and cover. Heat doesn't make it harder.
One attack a turn: shoot or punch, never both.
Bases touching? Those two can't shoot each other, but they can still punch or kick. Weapon hits don't weaken a punch, and overheat can't add to it. From behind it's +1, like a rear shot.
A punch isn't a weapon attack, so a 'Mech that only punches still cools off in the End Phase. Charge and Death From Above are not in this mission.
tableSteps: Use the same open table, about 3 feet across. Measure in inches and ignore printed hexes.
Put a hill in the middle and three patches of woods close around it. Tight terrain pulls the fight in close. Hills, cover, and woods work like Broken Ground.
The Awesome and BattleMaster share one card, front and back. Put that card by one of them and read the other's numbers in the app.
Keep a die or small token next to each 'Mech card to mark heat (0 to 3, then S). The app tracks it too.
Each side places its three 'Mechs within 6 inches of its own short table edge. After the first dice roll, the winner picks which side places first; then take turns placing one 'Mech at a time.
winningSummary: Knock out all three enemy 'Mechs. If anyone is still standing after 8 turns, the side with more Structure left wins. Same Structure is a draw.
